page: Amazon Web Services x8g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, memory-intensive server powered by 192 dedicated physical cores of the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor. Operating on the arm64 architecture at 2.7 GHz, this instance features 3072.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing 16.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1D cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache per core, alongside hardware-accelerated AES cryptography support. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional multi-core and memory performance. The server achieves top-tier status in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and passmark memory scores. Memory bandwidth is highly optimized, reaching 14555.46 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 860.6 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Multi-threaded operations perform exceptionally well, as evidenced by top-tier results in bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, software compilation with clang, and passmark database operations. However, single-core performance remains average, with moderate scores in geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core tests.

The server exhibits a clear tradeoff between massive parallel throughput and single-threaded execution speed. While it delivers top-tier performance in Redis SET operations (355.04 million operations per second) and static web serving throughput (148.87 GB/sec), its text generation speeds for large language models are relatively limited, with text generation for a 135M model rated as poor. Given its massive DDR5 memory capacity and high multi-threaded efficiency, this bare-metal instance is highly cost-efficient for memory-bound, highly parallel workloads. It is best suited for large-scale in-memory databases, high-throughput web serving, software compilation pipelines, and data-intensive enterprise applications.
